entries.p: Time represents an elapsed simulation duration, stored as signed integer microseconds.
entries.n: Time is different from Integer/Real. Time + Time and Time - Time yield Time; Time multiplied or divided by a number yields Time; Time / Time yields a ratio. Comparisons require two Time values. Logs render durations in seconds. Unit aliases sec/secs/second(s), min/mins/minute(s), hr/hrs/hour(s), day(s) are accepted. Plain numbers remain Integer/Real. Ordinary user-authored wait statements remain restricted by the current GRS syntax policy.

entries.p: Simulation Studio Model Logic source file.
entries.r: Init events, Vehicle event syntax, if / else, while, print to log
entries.n: GRS uses UTF-8 text. 2026-10-20: GRS was reduced to a minimal surface ahead of a full redesign. Supported: init events, model.snap, the 12 Vehicle events, if / else, while / for each, set / inc / dec, attributes, + - * / %, print ... to log, and all Humanoid events/functions. Anything else is rejected at Compile with GRS_REMOVED_SYNTAX.

entries.p: Runs after a completed Model session snapshot boundary. The event observes the model at the exact committed simulation time, without creating a UI render timer.
entries.r: model.init, Time duration, print to log
entries.n: The first event runs at simulation time 0 after Init. Thereafter one event runs for each successful forward ModelExecutionSession.advanceTo() call, after all physics modules finish. Re-reading the immutable snapshot, pausing, or advancing to the same time does not fire it again. Each module executes its own defined model.snap handler, if present. This is not triggered by Qt paint/repaint and it is not a request to save the project file. 'begin model snap event' is accepted as an alias. Normal GRS restrictions on wait and functions still apply.

entries.p: Runs once at simulation time zero to initialize model values.
entries.s: begin model.init event     ... end begin OHT.init event     ... end begin AMR.init event     ... end begin Humanoid.init event     ... end
entries.r: Global Init, set, print to log
entries.n: model.init runs once per model. OHT.init / AMR.init / Humanoid.init are the typed initializers used by Global Init.

entries.t: Global Init / default OHT AMR Humanoid
entries.p: Create the default OHT, AMR and Humanoid counts directly from one global initialization event.
entries.s: begin model.init event     vi_OHT = 10     vi_Humanoid = 3     vi_AMR = 3 end
entries.r: model.init, OHT.init, AMR.init, Humanoid.init, print to log
entries.n: New global-init script has exactly one model.init with three positive integer vi_* values and these three typed events. At Compile the already-placed drawing supplies one OHT rail Level and one AMR floor Level (each with two distinct Stations); scripted Job Source is used with no synthetic traffic. Existing C++ Core creates vi_OHT/vi_AMR vehicles. Three-dimensional default humanoids are created at a floor Station. The typed init events run once at simulation time zero and print to the Studio message log. Other legacy and previously declared auto-bound scripts retain their existing behavior. All five previous helper initializers are NOT required for this opt-in.

entries.p: Public Vehicle event syntax shared by OHT, AGV and AMR: vehicle. followed by the event name with underscores (pickup, setdown, speed_change, resume_to_drive, start_to_move, arrived_at_station, job_finished, job_selection, job_assigned, decelerate_to_destination, passing_station, destination_change). The old space form (begin Vehicle pickup event) was removed.
entries.r: Vehicle, Vehicle, OHT, AGV, AMR, GRS Events
entries.n: The GRS compiler lowers these event declarations to the engine's existing internal callbacks. Existing project event keys still load for compatibility. The event actor Vehicle is available as this Vehicle. The same header works in OHT, AGV and AMR modules; steer change and for each ... in Vehicle are OHT only.

entries.p: Arrives at the physical pickup boundary.
entries.n: The Load is loaded at the existing physical pickup boundary. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: Arrives at the physical setdown boundary.
entries.n: The unloading completion occurs after the configured setdown dwell. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: Physical Vehicle speed changes.
entries.n: Uses existing engine speed transitions, not polling. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: A stopped Vehicle starts driving again.
entries.n: Uses a real resume transition. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: The Vehicle starts actual travel.
entries.n: Ignores the internal near-zero wake probe. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: A physical ScheduleJob reaches its completed handoff.
entries.n: Fires after setdown dwell. OHT: actor is the completed ScheduleJob (this Vehicle is its Vehicle). AMR / AGV: actor is the carrying Vehicle. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: A live ScheduleJob becomes selected.
entries.n: OHT: actor is the selected ScheduleJob; unchanged selection does not re-fire. AMR / AGV: actor is the Vehicle the Job was assigned to. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: The Vehicle reaches the final prepared travel span.
entries.n: Fires on actual movement in the final span. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: The Vehicle reaches its pickup or setdown Station.
entries.n: Fires once at the arrival boundary before the pickup/setdown event. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: An idle OHT begins its next Job or explicit travel.
entries.n: 2026-10-17: fires on Idle-to-travel/Pickup transition; actor is the assigned Vehicle. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: The OHT passes a Station on its route.
entries.n: 2026-10-17: fires for each physically crossed Station, excluding departure; no fleet-wide polling. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT.

entries.p: The OHT starts a new travel leg toward its destination.
entries.n: 2026-10-17: fires at travel-leg start (initial travel or post-pickup delivery), up to twice per Job. The engine uses an internal callback key; write the Vehicle event header in new GRS models.

entries.p: The vehicle.<event_name> header is the only spelling: there are no separate Def_OHT / Def_AGV / Def_AMR headers. It works in OHT, AGV (AMR Core Fixed Path) and AMR modules with the same 12 event names.
entries.r: Vehicle, AMR, AGV, OHT, GRS Events
entries.n: Observation is enabled only for events you implement and never changes physics. This Vehicle is the actor Vehicle. passing station radius for AMR / AGV is max(250 mm, body radius); vehicle.passing_station_name reads the station just passed. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT. for each ... in Vehicle is OHT only: an AMR / AGV module that uses it is rejected before the run.

entries.p: Humanoid uses the same 12 event names (begin humanoid.pickup event, ...). Job means humanoid_transfer; pickup/setdown fire when humanoid_pick/humanoid_place start.
entries.n: this Humanoid is humanoid_self(); humanoid_event_place() reads the place just passed (within 400 mm) inside passing station. resume to drive occurs only in live walking. wait is not allowed inside a passing station event (the vehicle is moving through the Station): compile error GRS_SEMA_WAIT_IN_PASSING_STATION_EVENT.

entries.p: Run starts OHT 10, AMR 3 and Humanoid 3 and drives Humanoid 1 and 2 back and forth through physical floor Stations.
entries.r: Humanoid.init, humanoid.arrived, humanoid_create, humanoid_walk_to, print to log
entries.n: Opt-in requires two GRS files: model_init.grs with vi_OHT, vi_AMR, vi_Humanoid and OHT.init, AMR.init, Humanoid.init; and humanoid_logic.grs with walk resume/start/arrived at station events. All three Init callbacks must complete across all modules before any regular t=0 event or initial humanoid walk begins. A waiting/failed Init rejects Run before simulation time advances. In model_init.grs the authored spwan Humanoid(1 or 2) to humanoid_1 or humanoid_2 is accepted as compatibility syntax. These compile to native humanoid_create, humanoid_walk_to, humanoid.arrived and a suspended 0.5-second wait. Each physical arrival triggers the next leg, without every-event polling. Humanoid 3 remains idle until explicitly dispatched; Job flows removed from this project are not auto restored. Existing auto-bound and explicitly declared module behavior is unchanged.

entries.p: Creates a Humanoid at a Station/defined place or x/y (m).

entries.t: Humanoid_Define_Place(name, work_height_mm | name, x_m, y_m [, work_height_mm])
entries.p: Defines a named work place for humanoid_walk_to/pick/place. Station form (name, work_height_mm) takes position/level from the Station of that name, so no coordinates are written in GRS.
entries.s: call Humanoid_Define_Place(name, work_height_mm | name, x_m, y_m [, work_height_mm])
entries.n: Defined places win over Station names. Default work height is 900 mm. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_place().

entries.t: Humanoid_Define_Obstacle(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, level_id [, z_min_m [, z_max_m]]])
entries.p: Defines a rectangular obstacle Humanoids walk around (optionally limited to a height range).
entries.s: call Humanoid_Define_Obstacle(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, level_id [, z_min_m [, z_max_m]]])
entries.n: On a level with at least one obstacle, humanoid_walk_to/walk/transfer plan a detour (AMR grid A*, body half-width + 50 mm clearance) and use its length x route_factor. Levels without obstacles keep straight-line x route_factor. A walk with no route is rejected. Already planned walks are not re-planned. Height range (default floor to ceiling): an obstacle blocks a Humanoid only if z_max > 0.1 m and z_min < its height, so a low curb is stepped over and an overhead beam is walked under. AMR positions at request time are treated as temporary obstacles on the walk. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_obstacle().

entries.p: Removes an obstacle (true if it existed).
entries.n: Affects walks requested afterwards. Implementation spelling: humanoid_remove_obstacle().

entries.t: Humanoid_Define_Zone(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, capacity [, level_id]])
entries.p: Defines a corridor/area that at most `capacity` (default 1) Humanoids may be walking through at once.
entries.s: call Humanoid_Define_Zone(name, x1_m, y1_m, x2_m, y2_m [, capacity [, level_id]])
entries.n: A Humanoid entering from outside waits at the entrance until the zone has room (first-requested first-served). Only walking time inside the zone is counted; standing Humanoids and other vehicle types do not occupy it. Zones on one level must not overlap. Implementation spelling: humanoid_define_zone().
